problem: Network setup quotations contain unrelated page context and omit a relevant cross-page continuation.
evidence: NET-023 quotes software/firmware signing Table 2 and surrounding p029:u001, MACsec XPN p020:u004, Red AW p026:u002, and unrelated management p030:u003/u005/u007. Its certificate provisioning quote reaches p029:u013 but omits p030:u001 continuation for the CA response and certificate installation. NET-016 includes relocated rows MSC-DM-15/16/18/19/20/21 as setup. ROOT-NET-001 is fixed for NET-001 but the same page/block selection problem remains elsewhere.
proposed_correction: Select relevant complete prose blocks and contextualized requirement rows by meaning. Include cross-page continuations. Remove or separately label unrelated general context; audit all examples for the same pattern.
resolution: Verified NET-023 now uses relevant authentication/provisioning blocks, includes p030:u001.s002-s007, and excludes unrelated firmware signing, XPN, and Red AW blocks. NET-016 uses exact requirement-ID matching and excludes relocated neighboring rows.

problem: An extracted fact narrows Red time-source placement beyond the source requirement.
evidence: MSC-SR-3 requires a trusted time source located in the Red Network. Only MSC-SR-4 specifies the Gray Management Network. NET-026 facts and ROLE-trusted-time-source description instead say Red and Gray Management Networks.
proposed_correction: State Red Network for SR-3 and Gray Management Network for SR-4. Preserve the different scopes in roles and network facts.
resolution: Verified NET-026 and ROLE-trusted-time-source preserve Red Network versus Gray Management Network placement.

problem: Specified relationships and Gray network context are absent from structured network fields.
evidence: NET-011 through NET-027 all have empty networks, links, interfaces, and sites_and_boundaries fields, including NET-015 which explicitly describes alternative screening-router placement on the Black Network outside the solution and NET-017 which explicitly describes a serial connection from Gray AW to Outer Encryption Component. Figure 5 visibly labels shared Gray Data Network segments, but NET-005 networks includes only Red and Black networks.
proposed_correction: Encode source-stated placements, roles, flows, and conditional relationships without inventing full physical links. Model stated alternatives explicitly. Preserve visible Gray Data Network segments and known solution-boundary facts, distinguishing visual interpretation from source text.
resolution: Verified source-stated conditional relationships, placement and configuration alternatives in NET-011 through NET-027. NET-005 now records both Gray Data Network segments and their shared connectivity.

problem: Full-document role candidates outside the examples lack any recorded disposition.
evidence: The original mentions an approved password generator in MSC-GD-21, a SIEM or similar log/status repository in section 4.1.4, testing equipment/software in the Gray Box Testing definition, and a backup storage medium in MSC-GD-15. None appears as a role, unresolved candidate, or explicit exclusion in the reviewed inventory.
proposed_correction: Add supported device/service roles for password generation and log repositories. Classify testing equipment and storage media with an explicit role, unresolved entry, or reasoned exclusion that defines inventory scope. Avoid equating an approved password generator with an NSA-approved KGS without evidence.
resolution: Verified password-generator, log-repository, testing-equipment and testing-software roles have exact source evidence. Backup storage medium has a reasoned storage-asset exclusion.

problem: Outer VPN filtering is represented as an HTTP endpoint.
evidence: The initial relationship revision links Outer VPN Gateway directly to CDP as an HTTP revocation participant. PF-15 instead requires its Gray interfaces to allow request/reply traffic between Inner VPN Gateways and CDPs/OCSP Responders.
proposed_correction: Keep the Inner-to-revocation-service exchange and model Outer as filtering/transit only.
resolution: Verified no Outer-to-CDP revocation-endpoint edge remains. NET-025 records Inner-to-CDP traffic and identifies Outer as transit/filter component.

problem: The revised unknown-placement statement discards a stated conditional Inner Firewall position.
evidence: NET-019 claims placement and interfaces are not specified here despite section 5.6 placing Inner Firewall between the Red Network and Inner Encryption Component.
proposed_correction: Preserve that conditional placement when an Inner Firewall is used. Limit unknown details to the other CP and unspecified implementation.
resolution: Verified NET-019 includes the conditional Red Network / Inner Firewall / Inner Encryption Component placement; unknown companion-CP details remain qualified.

problem: Whole-solution egress is represented as one Solution Component device.
evidence: NET-018 uses a physical_egress_path edge to NET-018-solution-component for the source footnote egress via a CSfC Solution conforming to a CP. The source describes a solution/path, not an individual device.
proposed_correction: Represent a CP-conforming solution as an aggregate or an egress-path alternative and remove unsupported component identity.
resolution: Verified NET-018 uses a solution_aggregate endpoint for CP-conforming egress and removes the unsupported single Solution Component device.

problem: Role aliases assert identity beyond the quoted source.
evidence: Root CA is an example of a trust anchor in provisioning, but Trust Anchor CA is listed as an exact Root CA alias. The compound CDP/OCSP is listed as an OCSP Responder alias although it names alternative or combined revocation functions.
proposed_correction: Separate Root CA from Trust Anchor CA or mark the alias uncertain with full example context. Retain CDP/OCSP as compound source wording mapped to the relevant roles, not a synonym.
resolution: Verified Root CA and Trust Anchor CA are separate roles with example scope stated. CDP/OCSP is no longer an OCSP synonym; compound wording remains in source evidence.

problem: The theorem wording promotes recommendations to unqualified behavior.
evidence: RG-002 says proposed modifications are assessed through vendor and NIAP continuity process, while source says customers should engage/consult. RG-050 says SIEMs use the recommended log transport, while source says log data should be encrypted. Force metadata recognizes recommendations.
proposed_correction: Make recommendation strength explicit within each theorem statement; keep mandatory NIAP statement and conditional SIEM duties distinct.
resolution: Verified RG-002 and RG-050 theorem statements explicitly retain consultation/log-encryption recommendation strength.

problem: The universal KGS theorem silently omits the EAP-TLS CAK derivation tension.
evidence: The source says EAP-TLS derives CAK from MSK, then says all CAKs/CKNs are generated by KGS. Initial RG-027 asserted KGS provenance universally without an open issue.
proposed_correction: Retain both passages, record the source ambiguity, and keep the theorem provisional with explicit authentication-branch scope. Do not invent precedence.
resolution: Verified RG-027 is provisional for EAP-TLS CAK provenance and REQ-I15 links both conflicting source passages. The source ambiguity remains unresolved and blocks unqualified formalization.

problem: The theorem assigns variant approval engagement to the wrong actor.
evidence: The initial theorem makes the AO handle variants through NSA engagement, but the source says customers who want a variant contact their NSA External Engagement Representative.
proposed_correction: Assign variant contact to the customer; retain the AO assurance and compromise-response responsibilities separately.
resolution: Verified RG-071 assigns variant contact to the customer and preserves the AO responsibilities separately.

problem: Outer Firewall local-address rules are conflated with Outer Component remote-peer rules.
evidence: The initial theorem says Outer Firewall applies Outer-peer addresses. Section 5.1 uses local Outer Component destination on the external firewall interface and local Outer source on the internal interface; OR-10 constrains Outer Component remote peers or other intended devices.
proposed_correction: State local source/destination firewall rules explicitly and keep the Outer Component remote peer condition separate.
resolution: Verified RG-035 distinguishes local Outer Firewall source/destination addresses from the Outer Encryption Component remote-peer connection condition.
